frontier.hypothesis: F8 (unchanged, now fully evidenced) — motion_Close is an escalation candidate: every sanctioned axis this ledger has measured is dead, and as of s7 all three residual mechanisms carry a backend-level disproof rather than a census or a narrative.
frontier.mechanism: H1 (16-byte outgoing-arg area, s7: compile-time constant applied by MAX on every call-expansion path; the only cfoas-free site, __builtin_apply, emits a frame pointer + 72-byte frame + 34 insns), F5 (ascending first-free hard-reg scan, no MIPS REG_ALLOC_ORDER -> $v0 not $t0), F7a/F7b (block-local scheduling -> descending saves and a filled delay slot). The s7 residual table shows these three account for 13/13 points with nothing left over. The canonical-asm endgame gate is a MEASURED FAILED gate (scan_hand_coded tier LOW 0/8 for both this function and its sibling, s6), and no coercion/spelling family has an in-hand SOTN-master precedent.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT self-dispose — exhaustion is the driver's call and this session's modality was forensics, not escalation. When the driver does route this to `escalation`, the packet is fully determined and both endgame-lock gates FAIL, so under the owner's 2026-07-27 standing auto-ruling the terminal entry is REFUSED / OWNER-ACCEPTED INCOMPLETE, citing the s7 backend disproof of H1 and the s7 residual table as the two load-bearing artifacts.

frontier.hypothesis: F10 (new, the only untried direction left that is not a body-level respelling) — a WHOLE-TU / file-level change, rather than a body-level one, moves one of the three mechanisms.
frontier.mechanism: Every form measured across seven sessions varies the BODY of motion_Close inside the existing ings2.c. The three killed mechanisms are all properties of how cc1 compiles a void(void) function containing a call, but two of them (F7a's WAR anti-dependence in the prologue block, F7b's delay-slot eligibility) are properties of the FUNCTION's shape as a whole — its signature, its callee-save set, its block structure — not of the loop's spelling. motion_Close and func_80083794 are the same crt0 open/close pair and differ only in the guard polarity and the D_800A2668 store, so the sibling is a free second data point on any TU-level change.
frontier.next_probe: This is a rederive/synthesis modality probe, not a forensics one. Reconstruct motion_Close from func_80083794's shape (shared static helper, different signature, the two functions written as one parameterised body, different declaration/definition order in the TU) and measure each with sandbox plus the instrumented cc1. Expected outcome is another kill — H1 is signature-independent and F5 is allocation-order-independent — but F7a is the one mechanism whose disproof is conditional on the function being void(void) with no incoming-argument copy, so a TU-level change that legitimately gives the prologue block a write to s0 or s1 is the one untried shape that could move a point.

frontier.hypothesis: F4b (carried forward, purely cosmetic, unchanged by this session) — reach floor 13 with a do-while(0) wrap depth below 3.
frontier.mechanism: The floor-13 form's only construct is a THREE-level do{}while(0) wrap around p's initialiser, which wins p $s0 by loop-depth reference weighting (p 10 weighted refs / live_length 8 = 37500 vs count's 34285). Depths 1 and 2 are measured insufficient (both 20) and depths 4-6 buy nothing, so the device is minimal for THIS body — but a body reaching 13 with a lighter device would be strictly better in front of a reviewer.
frontier.next_probe: Still only worth spending time on if a session is preparing a submission, which cannot happen while H1 stands (distance 0 is unreachable, so no candidate-ready is possible). Sweep bodies that lengthen count's live range without adding a count reference — an intervening real computation the target also performs — and measure score AND the allocno table (BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG=1). Success criterion is score 13 at wrap depth < 3, not a lower score.
